name: Deputado Luiz Eduardo Magalhães International Airport
before:
Salvador's airport, 28 km north of the city and the gateway to Bahia. It is run by Vinci and shares some of its facilities with the Salvador Air Force Base.

Getting in is easy and free. A shuttle bus runs every fifteen minutes from 5am to 1am to Aeroporto station on the Salvador metro, which connects to the centre at Lapa.

The terminal opened in 1998 and was finished by the end of 2000. It covers 69,400 square metres with eleven jetways, includes a shopping mall and is rated for six million passengers a year.

The setting is unusual. The site runs to more than six million square metres between sand dunes and native vegetation, and the bamboo covered road up to the airport is itself one of the sights of Salvador da Bahia.

A naming note for supplier systems. Locals still call it Dois de Julho, after Bahia Independence Day. It was officially renamed in 1998 after the politician Luís Eduardo Magalhães, which remains contested, and the operator trades as Salvador Bahia Airport.
after:
Salvador's airport, 28 km from the city centre. It is run by Vinci Airports and is also used by the military.

A free shuttle bus links the terminal with Aeroporto station on the Salvador metro. From there Line 2 runs to Acesso Norte, where Line 1 continues to Lapa in the city centre.

Vinci says it has enlarged and modernised the terminal, which can now handle up to 15 million passengers a year.

A naming note for supplier systems. From 1955 it was called Dois de Julho, until a 1998 law renamed it after the politician Luís Eduardo Magalhães. The operator trades as Salvador Bahia Airport.

claims.claim: run by Vinci Airports
claims.inAfter: It is run by Vinci Airports
claims.note: Checked for a 2025 or 2026 change of operator: none. The operator's live about page and its release of 17 June 2026 still describe the airport as part of the VINCI Airports network, which took it over on 2 January 2018; DECEA's live entry names the concession company (Concessionária do Aeroporto de Salvador). The operator's domain (salvador-airport.com.br) is the one in the Wikipedia infobox; OurAirports still carries an old Infraero link.

The operator's own figure, repeated in its releases of May and June 2026, so it is attributed to Vinci. For scale, the operator reports 8.1 million passengers in 2025 (held back below).

claims.claim: renamed by a 1998 law after the politician Luís Eduardo Magalhães

claims.claim: north of the city
claims.why: Fails the coordinates check: the airport is 68 degrees from the GeoNames centre, which is east (north is 68 degrees off, beyond the 45-degree tolerance). The operator gives only the distance, which is kept.

claims.claim: the gateway to Bahia
claims.why: A banned phrase, and no source ranks it for the state. The operator calls itself the 'porta de entrada para o Nordeste', a slogan, not a fact.

claims.claim: the Salvador Air Force Base by name
claims.wasBefore: shares some of its facilities with the Salvador Air Force Base
claims.why: Softened to military use (DECEA, Wikipedia). The Air Force's page for the base (www2.fab.mil.br/basv/) answered Cloudflare's 'Just a moment...' bot check, so the attempt stopped there and nothing else names the base.

claims.claim: getting in is easy and free
claims.wasBefore: Getting in is easy and free.
claims.why: Misleading: only the shuttle is free. The metro charges a fare (its own FAQ describes the fare and free travel only for passengers aged 65 and over). The free shuttle is kept.

claims.claim: shuttle every fifteen minutes from 5am to 1am
claims.wasBefore: A shuttle bus runs every fifteen minutes from 5am to 1am
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; neither the airport nor the metro gives the shuttle's frequency or hours. The metro itself runs from 5am to midnight every day (its FAQ), so a 1am finish is doubtful.

claims.claim: terminal opened in 1998, finished by the end of 2000
claims.wasBefore: The terminal opened in 1998 and was finished by the end of 2000.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The Structurae entry cited for the terminal answered Cloudflare's bot check, so the attempt stopped there. The terminal has since been enlarged by Vinci (kept above, attributed).

claims.claim: 69,400 square metres, eleven jetways, a shopping mall, six million a year
claims.wasBefore: It covers 69,400 square metres with eleven jetways, includes a shopping mall and is rated for six million passengers a year.
claims.why: Wikipedia's description of the 1998 to 2000 terminal, with no second source and out of date since Vinci's enlargement. The capacity is replaced by the operator's current figure (up to 15 million, attributed). The operator lists shops and restaurants but does not call them a mall.

claims.claim: the setting: six million square metres, dunes and native vegetation, the bamboo road
claims.wasBefore: The setting is unusual. The site runs to more than six million square metres between sand dunes and native vegetation, and the bamboo covered road up to the airport is itself one of the sights of Salvador da Bahia.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. DECEA's obstacle list does record dunes and vegetation beside the runways, but nothing read gives the site's area or mentions the bamboo-covered road (the operator's about, environment, tourist-access and passenger-experience pages were checked).

claims.claim: locals still call it Dois de Julho, after Bahia Independence Day
claims.wasBefore: Locals still call it Dois de Julho, after Bahia Independence Day.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone for today's local usage and for the holiday. The 1955 name itself is kept, from the law.

claims.claim: the renaming remains contested
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. Its only citation, a Chamber of Deputies bill at camara.gov.br/sileg/integras/17932.pdf, now answers 404, and the archived copy is on the blocked web archive.

claims.claim: 8.1 million passengers in 2025
claims.why: Held back: the old text gives no traffic figure, so this replaces nothing. The operator reports 8.1 million passengers in 2025, up 6.3 per cent (22 January 2026). Good sources disagree: Wikipedia's infobox, citing Vinci, gives 7,186,760 (up 5 per cent). Settle which count to use before adding a figure.
